messages:
maya: Quick proposal — TF change to tighten launch template tags and add a lightweight spot-interrupt lifecycle + weighted fallback list for the GPU spot pool. Trying to avoid large-scale throttles when a single instance family spikes. Details below.

simon: 👍 can you paste the terraform snippet and a rollout plan?

maya: TL;DR: add a `spot_interrupt` tag, enable instance metadata v2, inject an SSM-backed graceful-drain script via user-data, and change `instance_types` from a single family to a prioritized list with weights to diversify capacity. This is strictly a rollout to the gpu-spot pool launch template.

raj: How do we handle ENI/attach limits? Some of our models pin many GPUs per pod and we run into eni limits on warmups.

maya: Good call — plan includes a safety tag `eni-alloc=limit-safe` that our ASG scaling policy reads to keep warmup ramp slower for certain AZs. Also we'll reduce parallel node replacements in the canary.

natalie: paste the TF snippet you mentioned?

maya: Sure — minimal example: ```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_spot_pool" {
  name_prefix   = "gpu-spot-"
  image_id      = var.gpu_ami
  instance_types = ["g5.2xlarge", "g5.xlarge", "p3.2xlarge"]
  instance_type_priorities = {
    "g5.2xlarge" = 100
    "g5.xlarge"  = 60
    "p3.2xlarge" = 20
  }

  tag_specifications {
    resource_type = "instance"
    tags = {
      "env" = "prod"
      "spot-interrupt" = "enabled"
      "eni-alloc" = "limit-safe"
    }
  }

  user_data = base64encode(file("./userdata/spot-drain.sh"))
  metadata_options {
    http_tokens = "required"
  }
}
```

raj: That `instance_type_priorities` is not an official AWS attribute in LT AFAIK — is that Terraform-side logic?

maya: Correct — it's a wrapper we use in our module that translates to a `launch_template` + `capacity-allocator` map in the ASG/SpotFleet config. The allocator will use weights to pick instance_types for new launches and fall back when a family is capacity-constrained.

simon: What's the graceful-drain script look like? We need it to signal k8s and also upload logs to S3 before termination.

maya: Example user-data (kept short): ```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
# simple watch loop for termination-time
TOKEN=$(curl -s --fail http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/termination-time || true)
if [[ -n "$TOKEN" ]]; then
  echo "terminating soon"
  /opt/bin/drain-node.sh --kube
  aws s3 cp /var/log/myapp.log s3://redwood-spot-logs/$(hostname)-$(date +%s).log
fi
# install a systemd timer to poll every 5s
```

natalie: We should ensure SSM agent is present and the instance role has s3:PutObject and ssm:SendCommand. Add that to the TF IAM role change.

maya: Yep — new IAM policy will be added. Also plan to tag instances so our metric collectors (Datadog) can exclude drain events from service-level p99 calculations. Tag keys: `spot-interrupt`, `drain-in-progress`.

ops-bot: Deploy-checklist kickoff: run tfplan -> create canary launch-template -> roll to 3 AZs at 1% of gpu pool -> monitor evictions/coldstart -> promote.

raj: For the canary, please ensure we pin the AMI TTL to the same image_id used in prod so we don't mix old kernel + new script behavior. Last AMI rotation caused 502s.

maya: Will do. AMI variable will be locked for the canary and we will run a health probe for 30m: kube evictions, pod startup time, and SSM-run drain path.

simon: Any metric thresholds for abort? I suggest: if pod startup > 2x baseline OR SLO errors increase by 1% absolute, abort. Also watch for increased ENI attach failure rate.

maya: Agree. Adding alerts: `pod_startup_95 > 2x` and `eni_attach_errors > 0.1%` over 5m should rollback the canary.

natalie: How about cost behaviour? Diversifying into g5.xlarge will save ~40% unit cost vs p3.2xlarge but might increase variance in latency. Is there an auto-fallback to pick the lowest-latency family under load?

maya: The allocator uses a small objective: prefer cheaper units but with a penalty if recent tail-latency rose > threshold. So it increases weight for lower-latency instance types automatically for a short window. It's conservative.

simon: Final ask: include a terraform variable `rollout_mode = ["canary","gradual","all-at-once"]` default gradual and a `canary_percentage` var. That way we don't edit code mid-rollout.

maya: Done in the module. I'll open the PR after tonight's freeze window. Plan: PR -> single approver + eng-infra signoff -> create canary LT -> monitor 2h -> promote in 25% increments every 30m if healthy.

deploy-bot: Reminder: code freeze window active until 02:00 UTC. Non-urgent changes scheduled for 03:00 UTC onwards.

raj: Sounds good. @maya ping me when the canary LT exists — I'll watch for ENI errors.

maya: Will do, thanks all. :shipit:
